https://www.politico.eu/article/us-exclu.text: PARIS — The U.S. State Department will exclude French applicants from a grant program meant to support MAGA-aligned groups after Paris warned against potential interference in next year’s French presidential election. The program aims to advance the U.S. administration’s political agenda in Europe and fight what it describes as democratic backsliding, including “overbroad and vague hate-speech laws.” A spokesperson for the U.S. embassy in Paris confirmed French groups wouldn’t receive funding, as first reported by Reuters. Advertisement Advertisement The grant program was formally advertised in the summer after U.S. State Department officials held talks with MAGA-aligned think tanks and advocacy groups about funding opportunities earlier this year. That led French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot to warn against what he described as potential “foreign interference in [European] electoral processes.” The country is beefing up its arsenal to fight online disinformation and foreign interference ahead of the 2027 presidential campaign, with a law set to be considered by the Senate in October. A spokesperson for the State Department said the program “does not and will not fund political parties, in Europe or elsewhere” and added that the allocation of grants “was still in active deliberation.” The U.S. administration, most prominently Vice President JD Vance, has repeatedly framed the EU’s hate speech laws and election safety measures as attempts to curtail free speech and civil rights. Its high-profile support for Hungary’s autocratic former leader Viktor Orbán and its pledge to support like-minded “patriotic European parties” in its National Security Strategy have raised fears of election interference ahead of several key elections in Europe. The spokesperson for the State Department said the strategy objectives included “collaborating with European partners to jointly support European revitalization and civilizational self-confidence.” Nicolas Conquer, the founder of the MAGA-aligned French think tank Western Arc, has applied for the funding. He said he had yet to receive a formal response to his application. Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.ch-aviation.com/news/154963-.text: News Commercial Aviation Fleet News Commercial Aviation LOT Polish Airlines Airbus A220-300, © LOT Polish Airlines By Dominik Sipinski 16Jun2025 LinkedIn X Facebook Copy news link RSS Feed Type Scheduled Carrier Base Warsaw Chopin Aircraft 93 Destinations 101 Routes 114 Daily Flights 265 LOT Polish Airlines (LO, Warsaw Chopin ) has ordered twenty A220-100 s and twenty A220-300 s, with purchase rights for another 44 aircraft of the family. The contract, signed during the Paris Air Show, will allow the airline to move ahead with its long-awaited regional fleet renewal and the phase-out of its Embraer aircraft. Deliveries of the aircraft are set to begin in 2027 and conclude in 2031. LOT has also signed a contract with Pratt & Whitney Canada to supply PW1500 engines. The A220s will be the first Airbus aircraft LOT has operated in-house. Recently, local media reported that Poland could take a stake in the European manufacturer as a part of the ongoing reindustrialisation and decoupling from United States policies in the European Union. The Polish flag carrier began talks about its regional fleet renewal before the COVID-19 pandemic. Negotiations continued after the crisis and the Polish government officially confirmed an RFP for 84 aircraft was issued in early 2024 . In mid-2024, the airline added three E195-E2 s on dry leases from Azorra as an interim measure , but without prejudice for the eventual order. The A220s will over time replace the existing regional jet fleet comprising five E170 s, fifteen E175 s (including two operated for the government), eight E190 s, sixteen E195 s, and the three E195-E2s. LOT was the global launch customer for the E-Jet family, taking the first E170 in March 2004. It is the largest European operator of the E1 family and the eighth-largest globally, ch-aviation Commercial Aviation Aircraft Data shows.
